title: Potato, roasted, from fresh, peel eaten, made with margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato made from fresh tubers and cooked with margarine retains its natural flavor and aroma. The peel is eaten, preserving additional nutrients and fiber. It is a popular side dish and a standalone meal, commonly served in restaurants and home kitchens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Roasting gives potatoes a crispy crust and a golden color.
The peel contains more fiber, vitamins, and minerals than the flesh.
Margarine is used as a more affordable alternative to butter, adding a subtle richness.
Roasted potatoes are often served with a variety of sauces: ketchup, mayo, sour cream, or herb sauces.
In many cultures, roasted potatoes are a traditional dish for holidays and family gatherings.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C helps strengthen the immune system and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Fiber in the peel
items.content: Eating the peel increases dietary fiber intake, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Starch carbohydrates are rapidly converted to glucose, providing fast energy.

items.title: Antioxidants present
items.content: Potatoes contain phenolic compounds that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Roasting in margarine adds calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some margarines may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature roasting can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Margarine allergy
items.content: Individuals sensitive to plant oils may experience allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted potatoes are served hot as a side dish, cut into slices, wedges, or cubes. They can be seasoned with salt, spices, herbs, or cheese. The peel is edible and nutritious, so no need to peel.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked roasted potatoes in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness.
